_note: Plain-English reason templates for every transform (change reasons) and issue rule (issue messages). Placeholders use Python str.format syntax.
transform.phrase_simplify.delete: '{old}' adds no information, so the sentence is stronger without it.
transform.phrase_simplify.stock: '{old}' is a stock phrase. '{new}' says the same thing plainly.
transform.phrase_simplify.weak_verb: '{old}' hides the action in a noun. '{new}' uses the verb directly.
transform.phrase_simplify.filler: '{old}' is filler. Removing it makes the point more direct.
transform.synonym: '{old}' → '{new}': a more common word with the same meaning here.
transform.synonym.repeat: '{old}' → '{new}': avoids repeating '{old}' from a nearby sentence.
transform.transition_vary.replace: '{old}' was used {count} times nearby. '{new}' does the same job with variety.
transform.transition_vary.drop: Too many sentences started with a linking word. The link here is clear without '{old}'.
transform.split_long.cc: This sentence had {n} words. Splitting it at '{conj}' makes each idea easier to follow.
transform.split_long.relative: This sentence had {n} words. Turning the ', which …' clause into its own sentence makes it easier to follow.
transform.merge_short: Two short sentences about the same thing ({a} and {b} words) read more smoothly joined.
transform.passive_to_active: Active voice names who did it first: '{agent}' is now the subject.
transform.clause_front: Moving the '{marker}' clause to the front varies how sentences start.
transform.clause_back: Moving the '{marker}' clause to the end puts the main point first.
transform.opener_vary: {count} of the last few sentences started with '{opener}'. Starting differently breaks the pattern.
transform.contractions: '{old}' → '{new}': a contraction suits a casual tone.
transform.expand_contraction: '{old}' → '{new}': contractions are usually avoided in academic writing.
transform.voice_fit.transition: You often use '{new}' in your own writing, so it matches your voice.
transform.voice_fit.contraction: Matches how often you use contractions in your own writing.
transform.fix_article: Adjusted 'a/an' to match the new word.
issue.long_sentence: This sentence has {n} words. Sentences over 30 words are hard to follow; try splitting it.
issue.nominalization: '{phrase}' hides the action in a noun. Try the verb: '{verb}'.
issue.nominalization_plain: '{phrase}' hides the action in a noun. Can you use a verb instead?
issue.wordy_phrase_delete: '{phrase}' adds no meaning; you can delete it.
issue.monotone_run: {n} sentences in a row have similar lengths ({lo}–{hi} words). Vary the rhythm: combine two, or add a short one.
issue.repeated_opener: {n} sentences in a row start with '{word}'. Start one of them differently.
issue.repeated_word: '{word}' appears again within two sentences. Consider a synonym, a pronoun, or restructuring.
issue.passive: Passive voice. Active voice is usually clearer: say who or what did it.
issue.passive_agent: Passive voice with an agent ('by {agent}'). Try making '{agent}' the subject.
issue.hedge: '{phrase}' is a hedge. Keep it only if you really are unsure.
issue.stacked_hedge: '{a}' and '{b}' hedge twice. One is enough, or state it with evidence.
issue.weak_verb: '{phrase}' uses a weak verb + noun. Try '{replacement}'.
issue.weak_verb_plain: '{phrase}' uses a weak verb + noun. Try a single strong verb.
issue.expletive: 'There {be} … that' delays the real subject. Start with the subject instead.
issue.unit_spacing: Put a space between a number and its unit: '{fix}'.
issue.unit_case: Unit symbols are case-sensitive: '{bad}' should be '{fix}'.
issue.unit_plural: Unit symbols have no plural: '{bad}' should be '{fix}'.
issue.unit_mixed: This document mixes {systems} units for {quantity}. Use one system (SI) throughout.
issue.number_no_unit: A number in {section} without a unit. Add the unit, or say what it counts.
issue.abbr_undefined: '{abbr}' is used before it's defined. Write the full name first: 'Full Name ({abbr})'.
issue.abbr_redefined: '{abbr}' is defined again. Define it once, at first use.
issue.abbr_unused: '{abbr}' is defined but never used again. Drop the abbreviation and use the full name.
issue.figure_unreferenced: {kind} {n} is never referred to in the text. Mention it where you discuss it.
issue.figure_order: {kind} {n} appears before {kind} {prev}. Number {kind_lower}s in the order they're first mentioned.
issue.figure_missing: The text refers to {kind} {n}, but there's no caption for it.
issue.caption_gap: Captions jump from {kind} {prev} to {kind} {n}. Number {kind_lower}s without gaps.
issue.tense_section: Most of {section} is in the {found} tense. {name} is usually written in the {expected} tense.
issue.tense_outlier: Most of {section} is in the {expected} tense, but this sentence is in the {found} tense.
issue.unsupported_claim: Unsupported claim ('{marker}'). Add evidence — a citation, number or figure — or soften it.
issue.section_missing: No '{section}' section found. A typical lab/project report has one.
issue.abstract_long: The abstract has {n} words. Keep it under 250.
issue.generic.vague_quantifier: '{phrase}' is vague. How many, or how much?
issue.generic.abstract_claim: '{phrase}' is a general claim. Give one specific example.
issue.generic.results_no_number: A results sentence without a number. What did you actually measure?
issue.generic.conclusion_no_voice: The conclusion has no evaluative or first-person sentence. What do you think?
issue.generic.no_concrete: Several sentences in a row with no concrete detail (name, number or unit).
